Introduction and Purpose
Introduction and Purpose
Hello, everyone!
Do you want to play in VRChat wearing garments you've personally designed?
Create unique avatars with your own special designs.
It's easy with everywhere!
In this video, we will learn how to convert garments from Clo or Marvelous Designer into VRChat garments using Everywhere.
VRChat is a Metverse platform that allows users to create 3D avatars, interact with other users, and engage in various real-life experiences and games.
In this tutorial, we'll learn how to create VRChat garments using Everywhere, Vroid Studio, Blender, and Unity.
Before we dive into VRChat,
if you haven't gone through the basic tutorial of Everywhere,
we recommend you to learn the fundamentals first before proceeding with this tutorial.
Please refer to the link provided at the top or in the description.
VRChat Rule Guide
To create items in VRChat, there are certain rules you need to follow.
The production rules are separated based on PC and Android platforms.
For PC,
the mesh limit is 70,000, with a recommended mesh count of 32,000.
The maximum number of materials is 32, with a recommended count of 4.
In this tutorial, we will focus on creating avatars and garments based on the PC version.
You may find more detailed guidelines at the provided link.
Creating Avatar in Vroid Studio
Now, let's create an avatar for VRChat using Vroid Studio.
Vroid Studio is a free avatar creation tool provided by Pixiv,
allowing easy customization of Vroid avatars.
Please access the link provided at the top to download and install Vroid Studio.
Once installation is complete and Vroid Studio is opened,
click Create New and choose the desired gender for your avatar.
To dress your avatar in the created garments,
you'll need an avatar without clothes.
To remove default clothing,
click on the Outfit tab at the top,
and delete the clothing from the top and bottom menus.
If you wish to wear specific shoes and socks,
please select and equip them accordingly.
You can customize your avatar's face and hairstyle under the Face and Hairstyle tabs at the top.
Be cautious not to make your avatar excessively large or elaborate,
as it may increase the polygon count.
Save the created avatar for future use or modifications.
Click on the Menu button at the top right,
then click Save As to save the file in Vroid format.
Once your avatar is fully configured,
export it.
Click on the icon at the top right,
then select Export as VRM.
A window will open for setting export options.
Set Reduce Polygons for the body to 34
and Reduce Materials for Materials to 2.
Then, click the Export button.
When the VRM Settings window appears,
fill in the information,
select VRM 0.0,
enter the title and creator details,
and click the Export button at the bottom.
Please specify the saving path to save the VRM file.
Avatar Format Conversion in Blender
Blender Installation
Please download the file from the link above to install Blender.
For this tutorial, we will use Blender 3.0.1.
Installing the CATS plugin
To utilize Vroid avatars for 3D garments in Blender,
you need to convert the file format.
We'll utilize the CATS plugin,
as it's necessary for this format conversion process.
Please go to the link provided at the top to download the plugin
and follow the guide to install it in Blender.
Go to the top menu,
Edit,
Preferences,
Add-ons,
click the Install button
and open the downloaded file.
Check the installed CATS Blender plugin to activate its features.
VRM to FBX Conversion
Once the plugin is installed,
click on the newly added CATS tab on the right side.
Select Import Model, VRM
and choose the avatar file in VRM format that you want to import.
In the import window, select the option
Extract Texture Images into the Folder
on the right side to import.
Click on the icon next to Fix Model in the CATS add-on.
Select the same options as shown on the screen,
then click OK and Fix Model.
Once the fix model process is completed,
switch to pose mode to test
if the model has been corrected without any issues.
If everything looks fine,
exit the pose mode and click on Export Model.
Click Continue to export in the warning dialog
and save it as an FBX file.
We'll import this FBX file as an avatar into Marvelous Designer
and then dress the outfit on it.
Once you've finished creating the outfit,
you'll likely want to save the avatar file process
with Fix Model in Blender format.
This will be necessary for both the outfit
and avatar organization processes later on.
Garment Conversion in Everywhere
Now, let's create VRChat garments
using everywhere in the following order.
Auto-fitting,
Rigging,
UV Packing,
Texture Baking,
and Uplift.
Everywhere offers the same functionalities
within Clow and Marvelous Designer,
so it's recommended to use your preferred software.
Downloading Garments from Connect
The garments for the tutorial are available on Connect.
Click on the link at the top to access Connect.
Add the garments to your cart,
proceed with the purchase,
and then download the files.
Open the downloaded garment file in Marvelous Designer
and import the FBX avatar file from Blender.
Click on the link at the top to access the FBX avatar file.
Click on the link at the top to access the FBX avatar file.
Auto-fitting
If the avatar's size has been changed in Vroid Studio
and the garments no longer fit properly,
we recommend using the auto-fitting feature.
Auto-fitting automatically adjusts and fits patterns
to match the size of the avatar.
For a detailed tutorial on auto-fitting,
please refer to the link above.
The garments provided by Connect
are fitted to the default size,
so we will skip the auto-fitting process
and directly dress the outfit and avatar.
Rigging
Now, let's open Everywhere
and proceed with polygon optimization and rigging.
As the first step,
let's optimize the polygons
based on the polycount standards required by VRChat.
The polygon count for a single garment
including the avatar
should not exceed 70,000.
Please adjust the mesh count accordingly,
keeping some room for flexibility.
Enter the numbers and click Optimize.
Once optimization is done,
simulate the garment again.
Next, click on Apply
for rigging to start auto-rigging.
Once rigging is complete,
click on the brush icon to open the brush window.
Use the weight brush to make adjustments to the weights.
Before getting into weight modification,
change the pose and identify areas
where you need to adjust weights.
Adjust the blend mode and properties of the brush
while making modifications.
Use the sculpt brush to smooth out surfaces
or refine shapes.
Once rigging adjustments are done,
press the exit button to close the brush window.
UV Packing and Texture Baking
Now the rigging is complete,
let's switch to the Material tab
in the Everywhere window to work on the textures.
Before packing UVs,
you need to set the image size.
Choose your desired image size in the options.
Please avoid selecting too large sizes
due to texture size limitations.
Once image and seam size configurations are done,
click the Pack UVs button.
Set the packing ratio value,
choose other options if necessary,
and then press the Apply button to pack.
Once UV packing is complete,
click the Close button to return to the Material tab.
After checking the maps you want to generate
in Texture Baking,
press the Apply button.
We will keep the default settings.
Once baking is complete,
you can check the generated Normal map
and Ambient Occlusion map.
After texture baking is complete,
a corresponding number of materials
will be generated in the material list below
based on the number of UV tiles.
If you wish to have different materials
for each part in Unity,
please separate the materials.
However, for this tutorial,
we will not separate the material
and will proceed using one material.
Upload
When the garment creation is finished,
click the Upload button
to open the Export Options window.
Since we only need the garment,
please do not select the avatar.
Choose the necessary textures
from the options below.
Click OK to upload to connect.
Access Connect and download the FBX file.
When you open the zip file,
you will find the FBX file
along with the texture map files.
Organizing Custom Model in Blender
To upload items to VRChat,
integration of the avatar and garment,
deletion of hidden parts of the body mesh,
since Everywhere doesn't currently
provide these features,
we'll proceed with these tasks in Blender.
Import FBX and Fix Model
Open the Blender file of the avatar
that you saved in the previous
format conversion process.
In the top menu bar,
click File, Import,
FBX to open the garment FBX file
downloaded from Connect.
Keep the file settings on the right unchanged
and import it as is.
Delete the collection in the Scene Collection
on the top right.
On the top right in the Scene Collection,
you can see that the avatar
is imported as Armature
and the garment is imported as Armature.001.
Select the Armature.001
under Null and,
while holding down Shift,
drag it downward.
Since the transform of Armature.001
has changed,
select Armature.001,
then change the scale to 0.01
and rotation X to 0
in the transform on the bottom right.
Delete the unnecessary Null
at the bottom.
Select Armature.001
and rotation X to 0.01.
Set the options as shown in the image
and proceed with Fix Model.
Delete Body Mesh.
We'll remove the hidden body mesh
that is covered by the garment.
Select the body.
Switch to Edit Mode either
by clicking on Edit Mode in the top left
or pressing the Tab key.
If you want to select both sides at once,
press Alt plus Z
to switch to X-Ray mode.
Then,
drag to select the parts of the body
you want to delete.
Afterward,
choose Delete,
Vertices to remove the mesh.
Adjust the viewport mode if necessary.
Merge Avatar.
If deleting the hidden body mesh
is complete,
let's merge the Avatar
and Garment into one.
Select the Armature first
and Control-Select Armature.001.
Then,
in the CATS add-on,
Custom Model Creation,
choose the options as shown in the image
and click Merge Armature.
This will combine the two bones into one.
If the Avatar and Garment are merged,
let's check for any errors
by adjusting the pose.
Select the bone,
then change to Pose Mode
either by switching to it
in the upper right corner
or by pressing Control-Tab key.
Choose the bone you want to move
and check if both the Avatar
and Garment move smoothly when rotated.
Select the bone you want to move
and check if both the Avatar
and Garment move smoothly when rotated.
Eye Tracking and Lip Sync for the Avatar
can also be configured in the CATS add-on.
You can set up the Eye Tracking
in the Eye Tracking tab
and Lip Sync in the By Seams tab.
Export FBX.
When all the tasks are completed in Blender,
export it in FBX format.
Click on the Export Model
at the top of the CATS add-on.
Specify the file name and path,
change the path mode on the right to
Copy and click Export FBX to save.
Custom Model Setup in Unity
In Unity, we'll proceed with Avatar settings,
shader configurations,
format changes
and VRChat upload tasks.
Install
To install Unity,
please refer to the official
VRChat Guide link at the top
and install Unity Hub
along with the recommended version
2022.3.6
as of March 2024.
To set up VRChat Avatars in Unity,
you need to install the Creator Companion
provided by VRChat.
Please visit the link at the top,
download and install it.
Once the installation is complete,
choose Create New Project
and select Unity 2022 Avatar Project.
Set the project name and storage location,
then click the Create Project button
at the bottom.
In the next step,
click Open Project to open the project.
If the installation is successful,
you will see the VRChat SDK
tab in the top toolbar.
Importing and setting
Now, let's import the custom model file.
In the bottom asset window,
right-click,
Create,
Folder to create a model folder.
Drag and drop the FBX file exported from Blender
into the folder you just created.
If you drag and drop the FBX file
from the asset window to the hierarchy window
in the top left,
the avatar will appear in the scene.
If the avatar isn't visible in the scene,
press F to focus on the avatar
and adjust its visibility.
Select the model FBX in the asset window,
then click on the Rig tab
in the top right inspector window.
Change the animation type to Humanoid
and click the Apply button.
Click the Configure button to check
for any issues if it is activated,
then click Done.
Material and Shader
Now, let's proceed to set up the shader.
Select the model FBX file
in the bottom asset window,
then click on the Materials tab
in the top right inspector window.
Choose Extract Textures
and select the same folder
to load the textures.
If a notification appears,
click Fix Now.
Follow the same steps for
Extract Materials below.
This will generate materials
and they will automatically be applied
to the model.
Next, let's make adjustments
to the texture and material settings
for the transparent parts of the avatar.
Select the imported texture image,
activate Alpha is Transparency
in the right inspector window
and click Apply below.
Choose the generated materials,
then change the rendering mode to Cutout
in the right inspector window.
We will be using the Poyomi Tune Shader
as it is the preferred shader
among VRChat users.
Please download it from the provided link.
Once you've downloaded the file,
simply drag and drop it
into the asset folder.
Go back to the model folder,
select the material and
in the inspector window,
change the shader to the Poyomi Tune Shader.
After the change,
in the rendering menu,
set Cull to Off to enable
double-sided rendering of the garment.
You can adjust other detailed properties
in the inspector window
to create the desired material.
To upload an avatar to VRChat,
avatar descriptor configuration
is essential.
Select Model FBX
from the hierarchy on the top left,
then click Add Component
on the right to add
a VRC avatar descriptor.
Click Edit in the view
to adjust the viewpoint through the gizmo,
ensuring it fits between the eyes.
Once adjustments are complete,
click the Return button.
You can also set up lip sync
and iLook here.
If you select Auto Detect,
it will automatically recognize lip sync
and when lip sync is enabled,
the avatar's mouth will
synchronize with the user's speech
when using the microphone in the VRChat.
Enabling the iLook
allows users to blink their eyes
or move their pupils within VRChat.
To set up iLook,
click Enable and apply
the same values as shown in the image
for both eyes and eyelids.
To set up iLook,
click Enable and apply
the same values as shown in the image
for both eyes and eyelids.
Uploading and playing to VRChat
Uploading and playing to VRChat
VRChat Upload
Alright, we've completed
all the necessary setups in Unity.
Now, let's open the SDK window
to input avatar information
and run necessary validation checks
for uploading to VRChat.
Navigate to the VRChat SDK
tab at the top of the menu
and click on Show Control Panel.
Once the VRChat SDK
window appears, please
log in.
Confirm that the desired
avatar is properly
selected in the Selected Avatars
section. Enter the necessary
information in the Avatar Info
section.
You can set the visibility to
Private or Public under Visibility.
In the Thumbnail tab,
you can insert a custom thumbnail
you've created or capture
an image from Unity's scene.
Set it to your preferred thumbnail.
In the Validation section,
press the Auto Fix button to
address any issues automatically.
Once the configuration is complete,
go to the Build tab,
check the Online Publishing checkbox
and click Build and Publish.
Once the upload is finished,
click on the See it on the
VRChat website button
to verify if the upload
was successful on the
VRChat website.
If you encounter any difficulties
at this stage, please check
your VRChat account rating.
To register a new avatar
on VRChat, you must attain
at least the rank of New User.
Play in VRChat.
Alright, let's now check
if both the Avatar and the
Iron Man garments have been
successfully uploaded and functioned
correctly within VRChat.
To play on your desktop,
please open VRChat through Steam.
If you don't have Steam installed,
proceed to download and install
it from the link provided at the top.
After logging in,
navigate to the home that is
the default space in VRChat.
Use the WASD keys
to move towards the mirror.
Press the ESC key
to open the launch pad
then select the uploaded avatar
under Avatar, Uploaded.
Click the Change into Avatar
button to switch avatars.
Close the launch pad
by pressing ESC again
and move around in front of
the mirror to see everything
is functioning properly.
Press the spacebar to jump
and press C to crouch.
If there are any issues,
please return to the problematic areas
and
make the necessary corrections.
If everything is good to go,
enjoy playing with the avatar
you've created in VRChat.
So far, we have covered the process
of creating VRChat garments
using Everywhere in this tutorial.
Thank you for watching
and if you have any questions,
please let us know through the comments.
